newsitem.title: JAPAN: Court declares Osaka Teito Shoken insolvent.
newsitem.headline: Court declares Osaka Teito Shoken insolvent.

text.p: The Osaka District Court on Friday declared Osaka Teito Shoken insolvent with debts totalling 63.7 billion yen, private credit research firm Teikoku Databank said.
The firm, which is a nonbank affiliate of failed credit union Osaka Shinyo Kumiai, had 37 creditors, Teikoku Databank said.
Osaka Teito Shoken issued and sold mortgage certificates.
After Osaka Shinyo Kumiai failed last year, Tokai Bank Ltd agreed to take over the credit union's business.
In March, Osaka Teito Shoken received court permission to dissolve itself, Teikoku Databank said.
However, it was unable to get its lenders, which were financial institutions, to agree on the liquidation and decided to start the process for bankruptcy, Teikoku Databank said.
